utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we please have the case called.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is case number IT-04-79-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And the representations for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Alan Tieger. I appear on behalf of the OTP with Ms. Anna Richterova and Mr. Wilhelm Wijermars, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Stevo Bezbradica and I am here on behalf of the accused Mr. Mico Stanisic. With me here are Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic my legal consultant, and Tatjana Savic, my case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the regular Status Conference. The last one was held in June. I'm happy to see that representation is plentiful on both sides, especially happy to see Mrs. Richterova. We seem to be, on my reckoning, fairly well on time when it comes to compliance with the existing work plan. Some outstanding motions are pending, and we will deal with those. Before I go into that, I would like to raise, Mr. Bezbradica, the question of your filing of special Defence and alibi notice. As you are aware, as the Prosecution is aware, we asked for a clarification on your filing, and I think your latest filing was on the 15th of September, if I'm not misjudging. I would like to say that it could be said that it is a mere repetition of what you said before. Would you like to add something to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Under your order, we filed my clarification, but it is not really the same like the last time. And I would just like to explain our position about everything. I really apologise, but I don't like that you consider something in wrong way, because we don't like to make anything hard for you, and we are fully aware about our obligation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Sorry may I interrupt you. It is not a question of making it hard for me. It is taking your client's interest at heart, Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I fully -- I said under my submission in that filing, and -- but at this stage, in respect of special difference, we don't have any special difference. I just confirm yesterday's submission. In respect of alibi, at this stage we are in a difficult position because at this stage I don't have in my hand the exact name of the witness which I can provide you. I have my client instruction to offer to the Defence alibi, in that way I already explained my first filing there. But at this stage I can't tell you the exact name, the exact name of places and time where my client was at the time that the crime occurred. Since my investigative work would be finished, I will advise you about everything at a later stage and only at this stage I can tell you, Your Honour, about this problem. It means that by doing everything honestly, in my client's best interest. But for example if I tell you something, give you some name at this stage, but if my investigator is not finished his work, there could be some trouble for my client especially because I know that I have to provide to the Prosecution the right information about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, Mr. Bezbradica. Anything that the Prosecution wants to offer on this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe I mentioned this yesterday, Your Honour. I only bring it to your individual attention because it was mentioned before the senior legal officer, and that is the possibility of parsing-out the response. I just bring that to the Court's attention so that it may be considered. Rule 67 contemplates a number of factors, including notification of the place or places at which the accused claims to have been present, et cetera, and the provision of names and addresses. It may be the case that it is helpful that, to the extent a portion of 67(a) can be complied with, while other aspects are awaiting investigative attention, that the Defence could submit materials accordingly. On the other hand, if the Court concludes it is preferable to wait until the process is completed, then we leave that to the discretion of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, I will note on the record no special Defence is going to be offered by the accused. I don't think we have that on the record before, but we note that now. Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes. I concur we don't have any special Defence at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Any light of the Prosecution's benevolent approach, i.e., understanding fully your problems, I think the best course of action would be for you to file as soon as you have the resources at hand and if you've done your research that you contemplate that you then file everything in this respect, rather than do it incrementally. Is that clear enough, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yeah, it is, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. If we then turn to the two outstanding motions we have. One is obviously of importance. Also the pre-trial brief to be filed first from the Prosecution then obviously from the Defence side as well. And I'm referring to the Prosecution's motion for judicial notice of facts of common knowledge and adjudicated facts and we have had a impressive number of facts from the Prosecution. We also, Mr. Bezbradica, obviously have your response, and there seems to be a gap between the two, i.e., you, if I have my calculations right, do not object to judicial notice taken of some 86 adjudicated facts out of, I think, some 700 plus. This is a point, I think, of importance and I understand this was also raised and touched upon at some length during the 65 ter conference yesterday. The position the Chamber takes at this point is first one of clarification, I think it's in need from the Prosecution side to clarify the issue on those claimed adjudicated facts which are subject to appeal. In order for the Chamber to, obviously depending on the response from the accused, to assess this fully, I think it is needed to have some clear linkage between various portions of the judgements under appeal, and the facts adjudicated in order for us to make a proper assessment. Do you care to comment on that now, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would be pleased to, Your Honour. As the Court indicated, that matter was raised yesterday at the 65 ter conference. At that time I advised Mr. Cubbon that I understood paragraph 26 as specifying precisely the basis that he articulated during the conference, that is that none of the adjudicated -- of the specified adjudicated facts were the subject of challenge in any of the pending appeals, and, therefore the appellate process would not affect those -- the adjudication of those facts. I indicated, however, that I would confirm that my reading of paragraph 26 and my understanding was accurate, and I have done so. Ms. Richterova and I related that to our learned friends today, during a conference, and they are now aware of the fact that all of the listed facts adjudicated in the Brdjanin, Galic and Simic case are not the subject of challenge in those appeals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your comment to that, Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday already we gave our submission -- our position in respect of this, this issue. But at this stage, just a short comment I put already my submission everything, and my position is supported by the recent -- the Court decision like in the Prlic test or Krajisnik test and under our opinion, these facts, which are subject on appeal can be considered by the Court as adjudicated facts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I also have the question, Mr. Tieger, of supporting documents when it relates to the two facts of common knowledge which you put forward. I think, unless Mr. Bezbradica is happy to proceed on the basis that they're absent, I think it would be helpful if you could file those documents as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Footnotes 13 to 15, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I completely agree, Your Honour. In fact we provided those documents to the Defence during the meeting I mentioned earlier and we have those here with us today to provide to the Court and the Registry as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I take it by your body language, Mr. Bezbradica, that you agree that that is a fact at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This afternoon Ms. Richterova gave to me everything, and she pointed everything that is -- what she put in the motion, in these materials. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I, with the Court's indulgence, focus a bit further, for two reasons on the ajudicated-fact issue. Number 1, just for purposes of clarification, I see that the record indicates that Mr. Bezbradica said in reference to the Prlic test or the Krajisnik test that it's the Defence opinion that facts which are subject -- that those facts which are subject on appeal can be considered by the Court as adjudicated facts. I think the dispute, as it currently exists between the parties now is that there is no longer any question that the Prosecution attempted to identify facts from those three cases which are not in dispute. The Defence understands that but says, nevertheless, its position is that those facts should not be considered until the appellate process has been completed. So I think that is the dispute that the Court will have to consider. I would only mention that it is my recollection of the Krajisnik case -- and I haven't done the -- haven't looked since yesterday's discussion at the particular facts at issue there -- that facts from earlier cases which were not in dispute during the appellant process were considered. I would also say that we will also be bringing to the Defence's attention other aspects of their motion which we consider misplaced, and that would include the following: There is an assertion that a number of the adjudicated facts reflect legal conclusions, rather than factual assertions. Again, our review of those facts seems to indicate the contrary. I refer, for example, to facts simply identifying the destruction of mosques or buildings. There is an assertion that certain adjudicated facts do not precisely reflect the language of the judgement itself. Again, to the extent we've checked that, that assertion appears to be contradicted by the exact correspondence between the language in the listed adjudicated facts and the language of the judgement itself. But we will bring those specific issues to the attention of the Defence and hopefully, since that appears to be the basis for rejection of those particular adjudicated facts, it will bridge the gap further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger, for underscoring and clarifying these points. The way the Chamber sees this at the moment is two perspectives. One is obviously efforts should be made to try to come to an agreement on this whole area, i.e., both the facts of common knowledge which are in dispute as well as adjudicated facts, and try to transform them into agreed facts in general. As we now stand, I think we only have from the indictment paragraph 25 which is, as far as Mr. Bezbradica is concerned, is a fact that should be agreed. And I think obviously we should, from the party's side, try to reach an understanding to a large extent as possible. Obviously again, Mr. Bezbradica, in the interests of your client who is now presently on provisional release, once the trial starts obviously that will come to an end, if not before. And that means that every aspect of shortening this trial is something that is in the vital interest of your client, and I think that should be an encouragement for you to review your position on this. And I know that you are, or I understand that you are meeting with your client on Wednesday, and I would encourage you to -- to him convey the understanding that this is an important area which could considerably shorten the trial period. And hence, should be taken seriously, without compromising whatever legal position you're taking now at the moment. The second aspect of this is that once we have a clear, final -- well, nothing is final here, but at least as final as you can get at this stage, position on this area of facts of common knowledge and adjudicated facts, the Chamber will obviously try to have its decision on the disputed area handed down in such a time that it would be possible for the parties to take that into consideration while drafting the pre-trial briefs, because I -- this is obviously linked to one another. With that, I think a time period should be set for the efforts of the parties to try to come to an agreement and I propose and encourage you to file not only any clarification you deem to be necessary in response to -- the Prosecution in response to what the Defence has filed, but also report as to where you are on the discussions in this area, and that should be done not later than the 6th of October, i.e., Friday of next week. That will give you time, Mr. Bezbradica, after consultations with your client. And the fact that you may not be here in The Hague, I don't think should prevent you from addressing this and communicating with the Prosecution and vice versa on this topic. So any matter that you need to bring to the Chamber, including report on how successful you have been in trying to come to an agreement on this area, should be filed not later than 6th of October. Any questions on this? Mr. Bezbradica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Your Honour, just I would like to ask you for some understanding and if you can give us a few days more, maybe 10th of October, 11th of October, because it is true I'm flying to Belgrade tomorrow, and I will be with my client a few days. Also the rest of my team is coming there on Saturday and we will have, again, like team meeting and we will discuss everything. And I'm flying back to Australia on Monday. I'll be there on Wednesday. I will be really tired to fix everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I will give you the whole of Thursday. The 12th of October. I want to avoid the 13th which is a Friday for obvious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So the date is set for the 12th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And the extension then applies to the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand. If I could just make one observation in connection with that, beginning with our appreciation for the Court's efforts to make this process more concrete and the resolutions of disputes finalised. We did engage in a discussion, a fairly lengthy discussion with our learned friends today, attempting to resolve any misunderstandings about the facts identified as being potentially agreed upon. The Court may be aware that, for example, the Defence expressed some concern at the 65 ter conference that the Prosecution was seeking agreement on facts that would essentially amount to a plea of guilt. I think we straightened a great deal of that out and also identified a process for moving forward. I say that, not to undercut the Court's effort to move the issues currently in dispute forward to resolution, a decision I commend, but also to indicate my impression that this process can be an effective and continuing one beyond the filing of the pre-trial brief and up to the onset of trial. I think our continuing discussions will continue to identify issues that can be bridged so that the real issues in dispute can be identified and the trial cannot only be shortened when it happens, but that the time spent in trial can be devoted to the real issues, rather than to issues which, at the end, turned out not to have been disputed at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. As you said and I think I indicated, the matter will not be closed even if we try to bring it to a speedy resolution before the filing of the pre-trial briefs, at least the scope as it is now. That, I think, deals with the one outstanding motion that we had. The second one is a motion from you, Mr. Bezbradica, moving to have your present assistant, Mr. Slobodan Cvijetic assigned as co-counsel. Be aware that the Chamber is deliberating that and will hand out its decision on this not before long. With the outstanding motions now dealt with, I think it's proper, then, to review the deadlines that we now have in the work plan regarding the pre-trial briefs. There was a motion which was supported by the Defence from the Prosecution to vacate the order regarding the pre-trial briefs. It was denied last Monday. Do the parties wish to move on this? Are you happy with the times as they are now? I would think that if we now have a discussion which could be fruitful on the adjudicated facts and related areas and report on the 12th of October, I think it could be prudent and argued that maybe that time should then be changed to a later date. Do you agree, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And what I propose is to change the present times in the work plan and have the 1st of December, instead of 1st of November as the filing date for the Prosecution pre-trial brief. And in consequence, and taking maybe not due, but at least some notice of the fact that this is a holiday period, the time for the Defence will be the 15th of January. And as a consequence, the pre-trial conference which is now scheduled for January, would then - and this has to be confirmed, later determined -- it should now be reading February 2007. I understand that the parties are aware that this trial is presently scheduled to start not next year, but things could happen -- and I encourage both parties not to work with an eye to a trial at that stage, but a trial that could be had once all the preparatory work, i.e., the filing of the necessary briefs and pre-trial conferences that -- which could happen in 2007. And that's the understanding, because if every court -- sorry, every case was handled with an eye on bureaucratic scheduling take primacy, all of a sudden there would be a lot of empty courtrooms. So I hope the parties are well aware whatever comes out of the scheduling group which is dealing with it, with this, would take a second seat to the ambition of having this case brought to trial and be ready for trial as soon as possible. Again, Mr. Bezbradica, I think you would appreciate and your client would appreciate that that is the process we should take. Any comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, are you happy with this as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm trying to see here whether we have any other issue. Obviously we note that the disclosure seems to be of no concern. The Prosecution has filed 66 A(i) and (ii) disclosures timely and the Rule 61 (i) material and the electronic disclosure system is undergoing. So no, no comment I take it on that. That is satisfactory? I see nods from the Defence and from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I have no comment about that. It's consistent with my understanding as well. The only remaining comment I would have about outstanding issues -- and it's not an outstanding issue per se, although the subject has been broached at various times I noted it in my review of the materials -- and that is the efforts -- the efforts on behalf of both parties to identify the actual issues in dispute and, insofar as possible, focus and refine the case will be ongoing in the manner already described, and in a way alluded to during the 65 ter conference. And by that, I refer to a review of both the current indictment, a review of the upcoming judgement in the Krajisnik case, to the extent it may be of assistance, to either party, in focusing and refining the case, to both in terms of the crime-base and any other aspects that may be useful. So I'm anticipating the possibility of additional steps along those lines and, indeed, I noted also that the Court, in its initial written order on the motion to vacate, made reference to that as well. So we will be looking at those factors and maybe bringing suggestions to the attention of our learned friends and the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I am encouraged by this and obviously tomorrow we will know more about the Krajisnik judgement. Let me say that any direction that the indictment should take in this respect is an amendment to cut it down and cut it down to wherever is acceptable to the needs that the Prosecution seeks to preserve. But from the Bench at this moment, it seems that this area and these crime basis have been covered by a number of judgements and the upcoming judgement tomorrow will only add to that. And I think that will, as I underscored before, Mr. Bezbradica, encourage you and your client to take a serious look at possibilities of getting to the heart of your case. I can understand and no one is asking you at this stage to change your plea. Far from it. But obviously there are differences in approach which you can take in responding to the indictment, and I think your client's interest would be served, as would the Prosecution's willingness to review the aspects and try to amend it in a way which will serve the interests of justice. With that, I don't see any other issue, unless the parties needs to raise anything further? No from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And from Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEZBRADICA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. It means that we are looking forward then to the dates which we have laid down and the filings accordingly. And we will, if nothing either calls for it, have the next Status Conference within the regular period. With that, we now stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
